According to group theory, for a surjective homomorphism φ: G → H where G and H are FpGroups, the kernel is generated by lifts (preimages) of the relators of H. The method should: (1) Get the relators of the codomain FpGroup using self.codomain.relators, (2) For each relator r, compute its preimage using self.invert(r), (3) Collect these preimages as kernel generators, (4) Return an FpSubgroup of the domain generated by these preimages with normal=True.
nodes.expected_output: A new method `_surjective_fp_kernel(self)` in the GroupHomomorphism class that returns an FpSubgroup representing the kernel for surjective FpGroup homomorphisms. The method signature should be `def _surjective_fp_kernel(self):` and it should return `FpSubgroup(self.domain, kernel_gens, normal=True)`.

nodes.title: Modify _compute_kernel for surjective FpGroup optimization
nodes.description: Modify the existing `_compute_kernel` method to detect and efficiently handle surjective homomorphisms between FpGroups. The modified method should: (1) First check if both domain and codomain are FpGroups using isinstance checks, (2) Check if the homomorphism is surjective by calling self.is_surjective(), (3) If both conditions are true, call self._surjective_fp_kernel() and return its result, (4) Otherwise, fall through to the existing logic that converts to permutation groups. This provides a more direct and efficient computation for the surjective case.
nodes.expected_output: The modified `_compute_kernel` method with the surjective FpGroup case handled at the beginning of the method, before the existing FpGroup branch that converts to permutation groups.

nodes.title: Add sqrt_rational_rule to handle sqrt of rational functions with linear numerator and denominator
nodes.description: The issue is that `sympy.integrate(sqrt((a-x)/(a+x))/x, x)` returns an unevaluated integral instead of a closed-form expression. The integrand `sqrt((a-x)/(a+x))/x` is not recognized by any existing rule. The fix requires adding a new `sqrt_rational_rule` function that rewrites `sqrt((a+bx)/(c+dx))` patterns to `(a+bx)/sqrt((a+bx)(c+dx))` or `sqrt((a+bx)(c+dx))/(c+dx)`. For the specific case `sqrt((a-x)/(a+x))`, this rewrites to `(a-x)/sqrt(a^2-x^2)`, which can then be handled by `trig_substitution_rule`. The function must be added after `sqrt_linear_rule` and before `sqrt_quadratic_rule`, and `null_safe(sqrt_rational_rule)` must be added to both the `Pow` and `Mul` cases in the `integral_steps` function.
